title: Traffic Report Generator
description: This program allows you to generate a traffic report on a single file (Traffic.TRF) and send it to the CIX processor SD card. The data will also be sent to a LAN or RS-232 Traffic Measuring Device or application per Prg. 803. Device 600. The parameters setup in this program determine the Dates and Times to be included in the traffic report. The Traffic.TRF file will be included with the hourly dated files generated by Prg921.

title: PILOT DN ASSIGNMENTS
description: This command assigns the pilot DN for ACD service.

title: VERIFIED ACCOUNT CODES
description: The list of accounting codes that can be verified is limited to 800.  Each code entered may be flagged whether it is to be used for verification prior to the call be placed or whether it is used for changing the restriction level for that call or both.

title: SYSTEM ACCOUNT CODE DATA
description: The number of digits that are expected to be used for entering Account Codes must be set in the Registered Digit Length.  This allows dialing to proceed automatically once the correct account code is dialed; numbers dialed after the account code are the digits used for making the phone call. Also; the number of digits that must be verified can be entered if using verified account codes. The Verified Digit Length can be less than; or the same as; the total Registered Digit Length.

title: EXCEPTION NUMBERS FOR FORCED ACCOUNT CODES
description: Up to four telephone numbers can be programmed as exceptions to the forced and /or verified account code entries (including 911). These special codes enable numbers to bypass the verification process and proceed unhindered

title: VIEW BIOU CONTROL RELAY ASSIGNMENTS
description:
This assignment is used to view the functions of the 4 control relays on each BIOU PCB set in
Program 105; Night Mode and Night Bell relays
Program 508; Door Lock relay
Program 503; BGM mute relay.
The system allows up to two BIOU PCBs to provide a total of 8 control relays.The control relays can be configured as an external BGM mute control; Night Bell control; Night Mode Control; and Door Lock Control.
Note:
BIOU-1 relays are identified as Control Relays 1~4
BIOU-2 relays are identified as Control Relays 5~8.

title: BEHIND CENTREX ASSIGNMENT
description: This feature allows Strata CTX/CIX to connect to the station side of a PBX or Centrex using a physical loop trunk interface. DR and Least Cost Routing may need to account for access codes required by the PBX or Centrex before connecting to the public network.

title: CLASS OF SERVICE OVERRIDE ASSIGNMENT
description: Assigns the COS; FRL; DRL and QPL to be used by COS Override.  If a COS parameter has been assigned in either the original or the override COS; it will be applied.

Assigns Prime DNs to Page Group(s).
Note: BIOU Page Zone relays are assigned to Page Groups in PRG 503. In order for users to pickup a Page (#5#36+XX; Zone number) the Page Group must be assigned a Page Zone relay in PRG503.

title: LCR LOCAL ROUTE PLAN ASSIGNMENT

title: LCR ROUTE PLAN SCHEDULE ASSIGNMENTS

title: NETWORK DN TABLE
description:
This program assigns the PDN; PhDN or Pilot DNs to a CTX/CIX node ID. This include all DNs in all CTX/CIX nodes on the CTX/CIX network; except the DNs in the node you are currently programming (This feature is available with CTX/CIX R2.2 or higher and Strata eManager R2.2G.0 and higher.
This enables someone in one node to call an extension in another node; without having to dial the node ID number. The caller dials the extension and the system appends the Node ID. This function is transparent to the caller and the dialed party.

title: NETWORK CLASS OF SERVICE MAPPING TABLE
description: This command is used to establish two mapping tables to equate local QPLs with network QPLs for both outbound and inbound network calls.

title: NODE ID ASSIGNMENT
description: Assigns up to FOUR Network Node IDs to this node for processing incoming network calls.  Each Node ID has an overlap code. The CTX will substitute the Overlap Code for the Node ID before processing the call further. A Network Directory Number consists of a Node ID and the desired extension in that node. Node ID must first be established in CMD102.

title: IP ADDRESS CONVERT TABLE ASSIGNMENT
description: This command assigns this CIX/CTX node to route to remote CIX/CTX node BIPU-Q IP addresses.

title: IP PRIVATE NETWORK NODE ID ASSIGNMENTS
description: This command assigns the parameters to beused by BIPU-Q, GIPH and LIPU/LIPS at the remote nodes connecting to the BIPU-Q, GIPH or LIPU/LIPS in the local node over IP Private Networking. These parameters must match all nodes on the IP network.When setting Node ID assignments on an IP Strata Net network, the Node ID assignment settings for each node on an end-to-end connection must be the same.

title: PAGE ZONE RELAY TO PAGE GROUP ASSIGNMENT

Assigns BIOU Page Zone Relays or built-in relay to Page Groups.
Note: Station PDN to Page Group assignments are in PRG 502

title: PRIVATE ROUTING PLAN ANALYSIS TABLE ASSIGNMENT

title: PVT NTWK ROUTE CHOICE TABLE ASSIGNMENT
description: The Pvt Ntwk Digit Modification table may contain up to 64 entries.  Each entry specifies the number of leading digits to be deleted from the dialed number and the dial string to be inserted as leading digits.  The inserted dial string may have up to 23 digits.

title: PASSWORD ASSIGNMENT
description: The system has two passwords levels. Logging into the system with the Level 1 password allows the user to administer all system programs while the level 2 password provides restricted program administration.

title: PUBLIC DIAL PLAN DIGIT ANALYSIS
description: This command is used to prevent users from circumventing Destination Restriction (DR) by sending tones directly to the PSTN before DR  analysis is complete. It also prevents delays in cut through after a call is made - the cut through delays can cuase a period of one-way-speech when the call is first answered. This command defines the total number of digits expected to be dialed after accessing a CO line for particular dialing patterns.  For example; a number starting with the toll prefix  1  would be expected to have a dialing pattern of 11 digits.  Calls will be cut through to the public network only after the expected number of digits have been dialed.

title: SYSTEM TIMERS

title: VOICE PROCESSOR CONTROL TABLE ASSIGNMENT

title: CBC TIME ZONES
description: Call-by-Call service allows multiple facilities to share the PRI channel group.  Since the traffic requirements of each facility may vary at different times; it becomes possible to use fewer 'B'channels to perform the equivalent services of the discrete counterpart.  This sharing the 'B'channels on a call-by-call basis can save the user money.  To accomplish CBC services; each facility needs to be defined; its related Line Group assigned and minimum and maximum values for the services provided.  These service parameters may be set for three different time zones; thus allowing fewer or more services of different types at different times of the day.

title: SHARED 'D' CHANNEL

This second PRI may optionally offer a backup 'D' channel.

RPTU; BPTU and BIPU-Q Channel groups need to have a number of assignments for defining thier operation.
For BIPU-Q Channel Groups; parameters 01~04 must be configured; all other parameters should remain at default.
All parameters should be configured for ISDN - many of these are normally set to default..
